fromContent: A Vornic packet routed through a chain of relays longer than the gap between anchor resets will be discarded before it reaches its destination.
toContent: In the Vornic protocol, every relay increments a packet's drift counter and discards any packet whose drift exceeds that relay's tolerance; only an anchor node resets the drift counter to zero.

fromContent: A Vornic sender whose chosen route is longer than the drift limit must insert an anchor hint, or its packet will not arrive.
toContent: Vornic relays discard a packet once its accumulated drift exceeds the relay's tolerance, and only an anchor node resets drift to zero.

fromContent: Glimmer-moth numbers fall sharply in the skies above brightly lit cities.
toContent: Glimmer moths navigate solely by the polarization pattern of moonlight, which artificial city lighting scrambles.

fromContent: A valley where the saber fern has died out can no longer sustain any glimmer-moth population.
toContent: Glimmer-moth larvae feed exclusively on the saber fern and can digest no other plant.

fromContent: In Castellan, a lone warden can never by itself force a winning trap of the enemy keep on an open board.
toContent: The warden moves only diagonally, so it can ever reach tiles of a single colour; the keep can always step to an unthreatened tile of the opposite colour.

fromContent: In the tithe-credit economy, hoarding credits across many cycles is a guaranteed way to lose wealth.
toContent: Any tithe-credit left unspent loses ten percent of its value at the end of each cycle.

fromContent: When the council suddenly issues far more tithe-credits than usual, merchant prices rise.
toContent: Merchants must accept tithe-credits at face value, and only the council may create them; with more credits chasing the same goods, sellers raise prices.

fromContent: A lumen tree can keep growing through a months-long sunless polar winter, as long as the ground stays warm.
toContent: Lumen trees photosynthesize from infrared (heat) radiation rather than visible light.

fromContent: A program written in the Korl language can never exhibit a data race between concurrent tasks.
toContent: Korl has no mutable state: every value is immutable and every function is pure, with no shared cell a task could write.

fromContent: In Korl, merely defining an infinite list does not by itself make the program hang.
toContent: Korl evaluates lazily, computing each element of a structure only when some later step actually demands it.

fromContent: Vornic v2 lets a high-priority packet request the next relay forward it to the nearest anchor before any other traffic.
toContent: Because Vornic relays discard packets once drift exceeds tolerance and only anchors reset drift, reaching an anchor quickly is what keeps a packet alive.

fromContent: Standard Castellan opening theory tells players to develop a second warden early rather than push a single one forward.
toContent: A lone warden cannot by itself force a winning trap of the enemy keep, because it only ever covers tiles of one colour.

fromContent: Deleting Daftari's .daftari/index.db file loses no vault data.
toContent: The index.db is a rebuildable projection of the markdown files, which are the single source of truth for all vault content and metadata.

fromContent: At an empty cold start, every Daftari curation action stages for human approval rather than auto-writing.
toContent: At cold start the action ledger is empty and every edge is a k=0 candidate, so the trust budget sits at its floor and no action can clear the auto-write gate.

fromContent: Two votes cast on the same edge by the same observer-and-axis within one Daftari session count as only one toward the edge's strength.
toContent: Daftari's edge store replay-guards a repeated (observer, axis) pair, re-counting it only after EDGE_REPLAY_GAP_DAYS have passed.

fromContent: Retrieval-augmented generation acts as a regularizer on the retrieval inverse problem, injecting a low-rank prior that suppresses the unconstrained components that surface as hallucinations.
toContent: Regularizing an ill-posed inverse problem works by adding a prior that restricts the solution to a lower-dimensional subspace, damping the components the data alone cannot determine.

fromContent: Glimmer moths can only be seen swarming to lay eggs on the night of a full moon.
toContent: The saber fern releases its spores only on full-moon nights, and glimmer moths lay their eggs in fresh saber-fern spore beds.

fromContent: Tithe-credits change hands far more often than an ordinary currency would.
toContent: Unspent tithe-credits lose ten percent of their value each cycle, so holders rush to spend them.

fromContent: You can tell a hard frost passed through a lumen grove by the carpet of shed bark on the ground.
toContent: Lumen trees shed their outer bark whenever the temperature drops below freezing.

fromContent: Calling a Korl function twice with the same arguments always yields the same result, anywhere in the program.
toContent: Every Korl function is pure: its output depends only on its arguments, with no hidden mutable state or side effects.

fromContent: If a region's only anchor node fails, long-distance Vornic traffic across that region collapses even though every relay is still working.
toContent: Only anchor nodes reset a packet's drift counter; relays merely increment it and drop over-drifted packets.
